en: Points of Controversy,
Great Fifty-Section,
Eighth Chapter
Discussion on the Formless Element:
Are immaterial phenomena the formless element? Yes.

Is feeling (vedanā) existence (bhava), a destiny (gati), an abode of beings (sattāvāsa), saṃsāra, a womb (yoni), a station of consciousness (viññāṇaṭṭhiti), and the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)?
One should not say so... [and so forth] ...
Is there karma that leads to feeling?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is it to be said that there are beings who have reached feeling?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
Is it because of feeling that beings are born, age, die, pass away, and reappear?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is there feeling,
perception, volitional formations, and consciousness within feeling?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is feeling the fourfold existence?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
Is the formless element (arūpadhātu) existence (bhava), a destiny (gati),
and so forth … up to … the acquisition of a personal identity (attabhāvapaṭilābha)? Yes.
Is feeling existence, a destiny, ... [and so on] ...
the acquisition of a personal identity?
One should not say so ... [and so on].
Is there karma that leads to the formless realm?
Yes. Is there karma that leads to feeling? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is there a being who goes to the formless realm? Yes.
Is it to be said that there are beings who partake of feeling?
No, indeed it should not be so said …pe….
Are beings born, grow old, die, pass away, and reappear in the formless realm?
“Yes.
“Are beings born, age, die, pass away, and reappear because of feeling?
“One should not say so…” [and so on].
In the formless realm, are there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness?
Yes. In feeling, are there feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the formless realm (arūpadhātu) a fourfold existence (catuvokārabhava)? Yes.
Is feeling the fourfold existence?
One should not say so… [as before] … Are immaterial phenomena the immaterial element? Is there feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness in the sense-sphere element?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is that which is the realm of sense-desire also the formless realm?
You should not say so … [as before] …
Is that the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu) and that the formless realm (arūpadhātu)? Yes.
A person endowed with the existence of the sense-sphere (kāmabhava) is endowed with two existences:
And [is it] by way of the sense-sphere existence and the formless existence?

One should not say so… [as before]… Form-possessing phenomena are the form-element; formless phenomena are the formless-element. Is there, in the sense-sphere element, form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that which is the desire realm (kāmadhātu) also the form realm (rūpadhātu) and the formless realm (arūpadhātu)?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is that the sense-sphere realm, the fine-material realm, and the immaterial realm? Yes.
A person endowed with the sense-sphere existence is endowed with all three existences.
Is it by way of sensual existence, fine-material existence, and immaterial existence?
One should certainly not say so... [as before].
The Discussion on the Immaterial Realm is finished.
